principles.statement: Organize the learner curriculum around practical communicative can-do capabilities and scenarios rather than isolated grammar units or four-skill tabs.
Maintain an explicit prerequisite graph beneath each capability covering prerequisite capabilities, vocabulary/chunks, constructions and modality-specific targets.
For near-A0 units, choose one primary learning bottleneck or major new burden and support it with largely familiar language; treat the exact burden limit as experimental.
Integrate the learner experience around a common capability while preserving separate evidence by capability, modality, support condition and transfer context underneath.
Audit meaning-focused input, meaning-focused output, language-focused learning and fluency development over a rolling multi-session horizon rather than forcing all four strands into every lesson.
Treat any roughly equal Four-Strands allocation as a curriculum-health heuristic to test and adapt, not as a fixed 25-percent rule for sessions or stages.
Represent task difficulty as an explicit vector of lexical, constructional, input, reasoning, output, interaction, support, timing and context demands instead of one opaque difficulty level.
Increase task challenge gradually by changing a limited subset of major complexity dimensions at a time unless deliberate multi-dimensional transfer is the assessment target.
Use bounded planning, models, word banks and rehearsal when they make a target task learnable, but record their provenance and never count supported success as independent success.

Use comprehension and production as complementary learning conditions: make meaning processable, strengthen useful form-meaning links, then expand from supported retrieval to meaningful output and interaction as evidence permits.
Use meaningful tasks and scenarios as an integration frame where useful, but do not claim task-based pedagogy is universally superior or label language-focused exercises as tasks merely for branding.
Spiral important capabilities across modalities, changed contexts and delayed encounters over time rather than requiring all modalities in one sitting or treating one lesson as final coverage.
Unlock the next capability or complexity increment from prerequisite and transfer evidence rather than lesson completion, streaks or a coarse level label alone.
Keep strand balance, modality opportunity counts and curriculum coverage metrics separate from mastery, transfer and retention evidence.
Align assessment with the trained capability while changing content or context enough to test transfer; do not reuse the exact training item as proof of capability mastery.

Keep the capability graph, active-capability count, modality ratios, rolling balance horizon, complexity increments, planning dose, task-first/model-first order, learner-choice policy and capability-merging rules falsifiable until EXP-017 validates them for Vietnamese adults near A0/A1.
